extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and hearing officers
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative Final Order excluding a registered patent practitioner on an interim basis under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), documenting grounds for exclusion, notice/response deadlines, referral to a hearing officer, publication and notice requirements, and obligations for reinstatement and compliance with other regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), the Director of the USPTO orders the interim exclusion of the Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may order interim exclusion where appropriate; the Notice and Order informing Respondent was mailed January 9, 2009, and the interim exclusion imposed by the Director begins on March 13, 2009. Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion: violation of ethical standards 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim exclusion was ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), and 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific ethical provisions are cited as the regulatory bases for discipline; the Complaint supporting exclusion is based on violations of these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for exclusion: criminal conviction/plea
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for exclusion of the Respondent in the Complaint was based upon Respondent's June 15, 2007 plea of guilty to the crime of manslaughter in the first degree under § 53a-55(a)(1) of the Connecticut General Statutes and the August 31, 2007 order of sentencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner’s guilty plea and sentencing for a serious crime can constitute a basis for interim exclusion and referral to disciplinary proceedings under the cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a response to the Notice and Order within 40 days (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order directed Respondent to file, within 40 days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file such a response (as occurred here) permits the Director to determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact and to proceed with interim exclusion and referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to a hearing officer for a formal disciplinary proceeding (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5), to the hearing officer identified in the Complaint for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates the formal proceeding process under the regulations and assigns a hearing officer to manage the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written answer filing requirement with hearing officer within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date of this Final Order, Respondent's written answer shall be filed with the hearing officer and a copy of the answer shall be served on the OED Director in accordance with the instructions set out in the Complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must timely file and serve the written answer per the Complaint’s instructions to participate in the formal disciplinary proceeding; failure to comply may have procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish the Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette identifying the Respondent, registration number, interim exclusion, referral to a hearing officer, the basis (plea to manslaughter), and the start date of the interim exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides sample notice text and requires public notice via the Official Gazette as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to USPTO employees, interested federal departments/agencies/courts, and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of this Final Order to (1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (3) appropriate authorities of any State in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandated dissemination step to inform relevant governmental and state bar entities of the interim exclusion and pending disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties on suspension/exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 sets out duties of a practitioner when suspended or excluded (e.g., notice to clients, file transfer); the Respondent must follow those duties while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure: comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(e) should Respondent seek reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.25(e) contains requirements and procedures for petitioning for reinstatement after suspension or exclusion; compliance is necessary for any reinstatement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Service and address requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order and Complaint were certified mailed, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the last address known to the OED Director as required; the Certificate of Service documents mailing date and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a certificate of service showing method (first class certified mail, return receipt requested), the recipient address (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.35), and signature/date; proper service is a prerequisite for the notice process.
